title: Durrani Dynasty
capsule: The Durrani dynasty founded by Ahmad Shah Durrani in 1747 ruled Afghanistan and at its peak controlled an empire stretching from Khorasan to the Punjab; by the attested window of 1840–1846 the dynasty had been greatly weakened by British intervention and internal succession conflicts. Dost Mohammad Khan of the Barakzai branch had displaced the Sadozai Durrani claimants from Kabul by 1826, but the First Anglo-Afghan War (1839–1842) saw the British briefly reinstall Shah Shujah Durrani before his assassination in 1842 ended Sadozai rule definitively. The period 1840–1846 thus represents the final collapse of Durrani dynastic authority, with Dost Mohammad—restored by the British in 1842—consolidating Barakzai power and progressively unifying Afghanistan under a new ruling house.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial control during this transitional period is poorly attested; the boundaries reflect contested and rapidly shifting zones of Barakzai, Durrani, Sikh, and British influence.
